text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone proves nothing. All-female panels occur by chance, and research doesn't show same-sex panels reliably favour their own sex — sometimes the opposite. Raising it will read as a complaint about who judged you rather than how, and it undermines your credibility on stronger ground.

Your stronger ground: the unanswered request for written reasons. Chase that formally, in writing, with a deadline, to HR rather than the panel.

Also note what a *head of group* role rewards: client-facing ability and business development, not years at the drawing board. "Excellent client relationships" may be exactly the differentiator, honestly applied.

If the reasons, when they arrive, are vague or shift, that's worth pursuing. Composition isn't.
